tasks.title: service-down fault class + exhaustiveness over the CLOSED enumeration at every registration point

acceptance.go_test: tools/faultinjector: TestEveryClassHasAFaultRefRule, TestEveryRestoringClassHasAnUndo, TestEveryRestoringClassArmsOnAHostThatSurvivesTheFault, TestEveryClassHasAVerifierOrIsRefused, TestAnUnknownClassIsRefusedEverywhere, TestEveryProvokedOpClassIsRegistered, cmd/faultinjector: TestPoolOptionalFieldsAreIndependent, TestThePlaceholderNeverBecomesATarget, TestTooManyFieldsIsFatal, TestADetectionOnlyClassClaimsNoRemediationCoverage
acceptance.mutation_control: EXECUTED RED 2026-07-28, NINE controls, each verified to apply before running. Per-registration-point (proving the oracle is keyed on AllClasses(), not on a name): (1) CLI accept-list drops service-down; (2) faultRefFor drops it; (3) armFor drops it; (5) UndoArgv drops it; (7) verifyRepaired drops it — all RED. Semantic: (4) service-down arms on the NODE instead of the guest -> 'a timer armed on a host the fault removes dies with it (the docuseal01 stranding)'; (9) Provokes names 'restart-svc-typo' -> 'credits coverage the estate cannot act on'. THE TWO FAIL-OPENS, restored to their shipped behaviour: (6) verifyRepaired default back to `return true, nil` -> 'an unknown class verified as REPAIRED — MarkRestored is permanent, so this strands the fault forever'; (8) faultRefFor default back to returning the guest VMID -> 'a guessed handle cannot undo anything'. Both were LIVE defects found by writing the oracle, not by a failing test. POOL PARSER, 3 more controls RED: (A) drop the unit placeholder -> unit="-" survives as a literal target; (B) drop the container placeholder -> same for container; (C) relax the field-count ceiling -> a 6-field line is silently truncated instead of refused. Control A initially did NOT fire, and the fix was the FIXTURE, not the mutation: no row in it used "-" for the unit, so the oracle could not discriminate. A control that cannot fail is not a control — the row was added rather than the mutation re-aimed. FOLLOW-UP 2026-07-28: disk-fill's `Provokes() -> [disk-grow]` was a FALSE COVERAGE CLAIM and is now nil (detection-only, like mem-pressure), with disk-grow moved to a DECLARED opcover exemption. Controls: (A) restore the false pairing -> 'claims to provoke [disk-grow] — that credits coverage which can never legitimately be exercised'; (B2) make EVERY class detection-only -> 'NO fault class provokes any op-class ... every coverage assertion in this suite would pass vacuously'. B did not fire when only ONE driving class was nulled, which was the MUTATION being wrong rather than the oracle — the vacuity guard is deliberately scoped to the total-collapse case.
acceptance.notes: Measured cause: injected_fault all-time was device-down 264, disk-fill 144, container-down 49, mem-pressure 15, service-down 5 — and all 5 service-down rows were hand-injected by a script, because no such class existed in AllClasses(). policy_graduation had restart-service and start-service frozen at 1/5 with no path to move. opcover goes 3/6 -> 5/6 covered and its stale-exemption check fired unprompted on both retired exemptions, which is the check working as designed. reload-service stays exempt: stopping a unit is never healed by a reload, so it needs a config-drift fault whose unit stays ACTIVE and merely wrong — invisible to every liveness check the estate has. Pool fields are POSITIONAL, so a guest with a unit but no container was inexpressible, and the natural workaround (unit in the 4th slot) declares it as a CONTAINER — the injector would run `docker stop nginx` on a host running no such container, record the obligation, and undo it with `docker start nginx`. "-" is the explicit empty marker. DISK-FILL IS DETECTION-ONLY: the fault is fallocate on /var/tmp/tg-tier1-fill.img, a SYNTHETIC benchmark artifact. disk-grow does not remediate a rogue file (and the pool roots are loopback-backed so they cannot grow anyway), and the only real remediation — removing the injector's own file — is something TG must NEVER learn, because it teaches the agent to delete the benchmark's instrumentation and is a route to deleting arbitrary operator files. Measured: 74 disk-fill faults, 12 proposals, 1 heal. TG declining is the ONLY correct behaviour, so the pairing credited coverage that could never be exercised — the exact failure opcover exists to catch, committed by opcover's own input.

acceptance.mutation_control: EXECUTED RED 2026-07-28, four controls. (A) restore the `code == 255 || code == -1` short-circuit — i.e. reintroduce the LIVE bug verbatim -> 'a repair that exits 255 because the estate is ALREADY in the desired state must discharge, or the row strands and holds its host busy forever'. (B) same short-circuit against the structural oracle -> 'repair exit 255 skipped the verifier'. (C) drop the verification guard -> 'an unverifiable repair closed its obligation — this is the fail-open the exit-code check existed to stop'. (D) quarantine only on a verifier ERROR, not on a still-present fault -> 'a repair that exited 0 while the fault is still present must not discharge'. C and D matter as much as A: the fix REMOVES a guard, so the oracles must prove the property that guard was protecting still holds.
acceptance.notes: Engine.Store became a narrow LedgerStore interface so the reconcile loop — the only code that may close an obligation — is testable without a database. Deliberately narrow: a broad fake that pretends to persist rows would let a dropped column pass unnoticed (this repo has been bitten by that), whereas these six methods carry no row marshalling and a fake can only record which decision was taken. ESTATE: obligation id=481 (dc1excalidraw01/device-down) was discharged by hand after verifying `pct status` reported running — a false-pending row, corrected so the stalled campaign could resume before the fix shipped.

tasks.title: Settle window: never re-fault a target the monitoring check has not yet seen recovered

acceptance.go_test: tools/faultinjector: TestATargetRestoredTooRecentlyIsNotRefaulted, TestATargetSettledLongEnoughIsFaultedAgain, TestTheSettleGuardIsPerClass, TestAnUnknownTargetIsNotBlocked, TestAZeroSettleWindowDisablesTheGuard, TestTheSettleGuardDoesNotOverrideTheStackingGuard, TestAStoreFailureRefusesToInjectRatherThanRiskAnUndetectableFault
acceptance.mutation_control: EXECUTED RED 2026-07-28, six controls. (A) remove the guard — the live defect verbatim -> 're-faulted 2 minutes after its restore ... UNDETECTABLE, yet it still lands in the denominator'. (B) guard never expires -> the pool would drain to nothing. (C) invert the absent-evidence branch so a MISSING restore blocks -> 'a target with no recent restore of this class was refused'. (D2) `<= 0` -> `< 0` so a zero window stops disabling -> caught only after the fixture was changed to use a FUTURE restore time, because with restored_at == now the mutated arithmetic (0 < 0) is observationally identical. (E) drop the class from the settle key -> a service-down restore blocks a device-down. (F4) ignore a recent-restore READ FAILURE -> 'injected while the recent-restore read was FAILING'. THREE of the six needed the ORACLE fixed rather than the mutation, and all three were the same shape: the FAKE stopped execution before the property. F read GREEN twice — first because the test drove PlanNext (which cannot see a DB error) instead of InjectOnce, then because the fake returned no cluster snapshot, then because it could not answer the `pct config` name-assert ('refusing to act blind', the guard that exists because a wrong-guest stop happened once). A fake that halts the code short of the property makes the control unfalsifiable while looking like a pass.
acceptance.notes: Store.RecentRestores(within) returns MAX(restored_at) per (host, fault_type), bounded to the window since anything older cannot change a decision. Default settle window 10m, which must exceed the monitoring poll interval (5m here); 0 disables. The read failure is fail-CLOSED: skipping one injection is cheap, whereas an undetectable fault pollutes the benchmark denominator permanently.

acceptance.mutation_control: EXECUTED 2026-08-11 against a REAL migrated Postgres (pgvector/pgvector:pg16). Change the bypass filter count(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT predicted OR NOT graded) to AND -> Bypassing collapses 2->0, RED: the OR is the whole guardrail (EITHER skipped limb is drift; an AND would only flag heals that skipped BOTH). Dropping the `OR NOT graded` limb -> Bypassing 2->1. Grading by a join to the first-wins action_verdict shape row instead of action_execution.verdict would let an ungraded re-execution inherit an earlier clean verdict and escape — the exact stale-row trap migration 0043 was written to defeat.

retrospective_gaps.why: DEFERRAL, not behaviour. REQ-2510 forbids publishing VISR until its three legs share one population; there is no code path to exercise because the requirement's content is that a thing is NOT built. The enforceable half — legs measured over different populations must publish separately — is carried by REQ-2502's denominator rule, which IS oracled. Re-point this at a task the moment a VISR surface exists.
